transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Acme Eng Lead), Tom Garcia (Acme Platform), Sabrina Holt (Acme Security)

Summary:
- Main objective: plan rollout/cutover for POC -> pilot; discuss canary and A/B strategies, monitoring, runbooks, and security checks (KMS/SSO/SOC2).
- Agreed on next steps: Redwood to deliver canary playbook + smoke tests; Acme to provision staging networking and finalize beta cohort.

Topics:
- Canary strategy and traffic split (5-10% initial), rollback plan
- A/B evaluation metrics (latency, accuracy, cost delta, error rate)
- Monitoring and runbooks: alerts, SLOs, synthetic checks, logging retention
- Security: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency
- Dry-run schedule and responsibilities

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in — we wanted to go over the rollout plan and make sure the cutover steps look doable from your side.
[00:18] Maya (Acme): Yeah hi, thanks. we've been running the POC for three weeks, looks good. main concerns are monitoring and the rollback plan — we don't want customer facing errors.
[00:34] Raj (Redwood): Totally. I have a proposed canary playbook — start with 5% traffic for 24 hours, run smoke/synthetics and then ramp to 25% if green, and we keep an automated rollback if error rate > 2% or 99th pct latency above threshold.
[00:50] Tom (Acme): That sounds reasonable. what about A/B? we want to compare model variants for quality, but keep cost predictable.
[01:10] Laura: For A/B we'll do parallel routes, about 50/50 for a short window, but for production cutover I'd prefer a canary first then A/B for tuning. Also we'll share a spreadsheet that shows expected token cost delta per 1k requests.
[01:35] Sabrina (Acme Security): On the security side, we need to verify KMS integration and make sure audit logs are shipped to our SIEM. also SOC2 docs you mentioned?
[01:50] Laura: Yep, I'll attach SOC2 summary and our compliance pack. for KMS — Raj, can you confirm what logs we surface and how key rotation is handled?
[02:06] Raj: Sure. we write request/response metadata to audit logs (metadata only by default), and we can integrate with customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption. key rotation is standard, and we keep HSM-backed options for private deployments. I'll document exact log fields.
[02:28] Maya: One question — in the POC we saw occasional spikes in latency when batch sizes hit the upper limit. is that expected?
[02:40] Raj: Yeah, that was us hitting a batching boundary. our runtime does continuous batching so you'll see better throughput but occasional latency tails when batches accumulate. for the canary we'll cap max batch size and use a latency SLO to prevent user visible spikes.
[03:02] Tom: Can we set an alert if tail latency exceeds X ms? we want to tie that to an automated routing fallback to a smaller model or to our previous service.
[03:15] Raj: Absolutely. we can wire an alert to your PagerDuty. fallback policy — we support automatic routing to a cheaper variant or an internal fallback endpoint. we'll include the routing rules in the runbook.
[03:34] Maya: Speaking of variants, how does version pinning work? we want to be sure when we roll back we get exact model behavior we tested.
[03:44] Laura: You can pin model versions in config; rollouts are versioned and we keep immutable model artifacts so rollback is deterministic.
[03:52] Speaker 1: (muffled) also need to confirm data residency for EU customers...
[04:00] Sabrina: yep EU region concern — do we host inference in eu-west-1 for GDPR?
[04:09] Raj: We have region routing. for private deployments we can run entirely inside your VPC in eu-west-1. hosted will route to nearest region and we can restrict to EU-only if required.
[04:25] Laura: On the canary playbook details — propose steps: pre-cutover checklist, deploy to canary pool, run smoke tests, monitor thresholds for 24 hours, ramp and then full cutover. also include communication templates and pager triggers.
[04:42] Tom: For the smoke tests, can Redwood provide the script and expected metrics? our SRE wants exact assertions.
[04:52] Raj: Yes, I'll provide a smoke test script that runs sample prompts, measures latency and token counts, and checks deterministic output hashes for correctness for a small test set.
[05:10] Maya: Great. how about A/B metrics — what do you recommend as primary metrics besides latency and error rate?
[05:20] Laura: I'd say precision/recall on your labeled test set, user satisfaction (we can instrument feedback), and cost per successful request. also regression monitoring via scheduled evals.
[05:36] Tom: On the monitoring side, retention of logs is important — we need 90 days of request metadata. are you okay with that?
[05:46] Raj: We can provide configurable retention. long-term retention is an add-on but 90 days is doable for the pilot. note that full request bodies retention has privacy implications; we usually keep metadata unless you opt-in to full traces.
[06:05] Sabrina: We need to confirm which PII elements are redacted. also SSO — we want SAML for RBAC in the console.
[06:14] Laura: SAML SSO is supported and RBAC roles map to teams. I'll include mappings in the security pack.
[06:24] Maya: Back to cutover scheduling — timeline is tight, we want to go to pilot next week if possible. are these tasks realistic?
[06:34] Laura: If Acme can provision staging networking and provide the KMS test key by Friday, Redwood can run the dry-run early next week.
[06:44] Tom: We can try. I'll confirm VPC peering and firewall needs by Wednesday.
[06:52] Raj: For the dry-run, we should simulate production traffic for at least two hours and run failover scenarios, including an induced latency spike to verify rollback.
[07:06] Maya: Good idea. also want an A/B window afterwards for user-facing evaluation — maybe 48 hours of 50/50 for a small cohort?
[07:18] Laura: That could work, but keep the cohort small — maybe 10% of traffic in prod, or 50/50 within a beta cohort. We don't recommend full 50/50 in broad prod right away.
[07:31] [08:00] Speaker labels continue, discussion of runbook sections: pre-cutover, verification, escalation paths, rollback steps, post-cutover validation.
[08:15] Raj: I'll draft the runbook sections: prerequisites (VPC, KMS, SSO), deploy steps, smoke tests, monitoring checks, rollback procedure, post-cutover checklist.
[08:30] Maya: Can we include an explicit step to verify KV cache warmup to avoid cold-start latency in first-minute traffic? we noticed cold starts in the POC.
[08:42] Raj: Yes — warmup script that sends prefix requests to populate KV cache; we'll include that as part of pre-cutover. Also mention quantization profiles — if you choose a particular quantized model variant we'll list expected perf.
[09:00] Tom: For automation — does Redwood support running the smoke tests via CI (we'd prefer a Jenkins/GitHub action trigger)?
[09:12] Raj: Smoke tests are available as a script + API calls. you can run them from CI. we'll include examples for GitHub Actions and a curl-based script.
[09:25] Sabrina: Audit logs — which fields do you include? we need user id, request id, model version, error codes, timestamp.
[09:36] Raj: We'll include those fields plus routing decision metadata. full payloads are opt-in.
[09:45] Maya: Another operational question — what about cost controls during canary? e.g., hard budget caps or rate limits?
[09:54] Laura: We can apply rate limits per route and per-team quotas; during canary we recommend strict quotas to avoid runaway cost. we'll also surface token burn dashboards in the Console so your finance folks can watch.
[10:12] Tom: Excellent. on rollback automation — what's the TTL for routing change to take effect? we need to know how quickly we can stop traffic.
[10:22] Raj: Routing changes propagate in under a minute typically; degrade windows depend on DNS and client caching but for our direct API calls it's sub-60 seconds.
[10:33] Maya: Ok, that gives us confidence.
[10:38] [11:00] Short silence, then discussion of communications plan: customer notifications, internal incident channels, runbook owners.
[11:14] Laura: We'll add communication templates — email to beta users, status page updates, slack snippets. assign on-call owners for the dry-run.
[11:25] Maya: We'll pick owners; suggestion is Platform SRE Tom and Eng lead Maya as primary, Redwood on-call as backup.
[11:36] Tom: Sounds good. one more question — do you support feature toggles for model variants, like header-based routing?
[11:46] Raj: Yes, we support header-based routing and cookie-based routing. for A/B you can route by header and set a consistent hash to keep session affinity.
[11:58] [12:30] Sabrina: Security quick follow-up — will you provide a pen-test window? we may request a short security assessment before pilot.
[12:40] Laura: We can coordinate that. Redwood has a security questionnaire and can accommodate a limited pentest; we'll coordinate scope with Sabrina.
[12:55] Maya: Great. let's recap next steps.
[13:00] Laura: Recap: Redwood delivers canary playbook and pricing details by Friday, Raj delivers smoke scripts and runbook draft by Monday, Acme provisions staging networking + KMS test key by Friday, Sabrina to confirm audit log fields and pentest scope. dry-run target next week (TBD depending on provisioning).
[13:28] Tom: I'll update our internal calendar and flag the SREs for the dry-run.
[13:35] Maya: we'll identify the beta cohort and deliver names by end of week.
[13:42] Laura: Perfect. any other questions?
[13:46] [14:00] brief chatter, thanks and goodbyes
[14:10] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: moderate background noise at times, occasional mis-attribution (Speaker 1). Some technical terms transcribed with slight errors ("KV cash" instead of KV cache).
